references.text: Esau, who is Edom, settled in the Seir mountains. This verse confirms that Esau's descendants lived in Seir, as mentioned in Deuteronomy 2:8.
Esau is also called Edom. This provides background for the expression 'our brothers, the children of Esau' in the main verse.
The Israelites asked for permission to pass through Edom's land but were denied. This is why they had to go around Edom via the Arabah route.
The Israelites left Mount Hor by the way to the Red Sea to go around Edom's land, which matches the route described in Deuteronomy 2:8.
Ezion-Geber and Elath are mentioned as stopping places during Israel's journey through the wilderness, the same places mentioned in the main verse.
King Solomon built ships at Ezion-Geber near Elath on the shore of the Red Sea in Edom's land. This confirms the geographical location mentioned in the main verse.
The Lord had given the Seir mountains to Esau's descendants as their possession, so Israel was not to fight them but pass through their territory peacefully.
Esau's children who lived in Seir let the Israelites pass through, just as the Moabites did. This elaborates on the peaceful passage mentioned in verse 8.
